title: User–User & Item–Item Collaborative Filtering
interviewAnswer: Collaborative filtering recommends based on interaction similarity rather than item metadata. Item-item methods often provide stable neighborhood recommendations; user-user methods can suffer with sparse histories.
keyPoints: Cold start is a core limitation.
why: User–User & Item–Item Collaborative Filtering appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: Collaborative filtering recommends based on interaction similarity rather than item metadata. Item-item methods often provide stable neighborhood recommendations; user-user methods can suffer with sparse histories. Cold start is a core limitation. Implicit feedback needs confidence/weighting. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Recommend products similar users co-consumed, or items frequently consumed by users who liked the current item.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
